title: The one command four graded documents publish as proof of build provenance is false at HEAD
why_it_costs_marks: README.md:261, deployed.md:83, docs/pre-submission-checklist.md:43 (a ticked box) and docs/requirements-traceability.md:222 (inside the RUBRIC5.1 verdict, the top rubric row) all assert that `git diff 8a89310..HEAD -- src mcp Dockerfile render.yaml requirements.txt` is empty — the sentence that underwrites "the published evaluation figures describe the shipped build". It is not empty, and a grader falsifies it by copy-pasting the repo's own command. This is the same self-contradiction class the 2026-09-21 grade opened with, and the rubric's own language says a materially inconsistent evaluation claim typically caps at 4.
evidence: Verified at HEAD 2dee277 (clean tree): `git diff --stat 8a89310..HEAD -- src mcp Dockerfile render.yaml requirements.txt` → src/hrmosaic/web/static/app.css | 11 +, src/hrmosaic/web/templates/dashboard/evals.html | 7 +-, 2 files changed, 17 insertions(+), 1 deletion(-), from commit 3aa6650. Live /health reports git_sha 2dee277, which includes it. deployed.md:82 states the strongest false form ("8a89310 is the last commit to change application code"); CHANGELOG.md:931 repeats it. `grep -rn '8a89310' tests/ scripts/` → no output: nothing guards it.
fix: Restate all four sites (plus CHANGELOG.md:931) to the truth. The narrow form is already true — `git diff --stat 8a89310..HEAD -- src/hrmosaic/agent src/hrmosaic/rag src/hrmosaic/core mcp Dockerfile render.yaml requirements.txt` returns empty — so: "later commits change documentation, tests and one dashboard CSS/template fix (3aa6650) that touches no agent, RAG, MCP or deployment path — <narrow command> is empty". Then add a contract test in tests/contract/test_published_run_commands.py that executes the exact pathspec the documents print and asserts the diff is empty.

title: amb-001's clarification asks the wrong workflow's question, and clarification_accuracy 1.000 rests on it
why_it_costs_marks: This is the wave's headline fix and the one Section 4 bullet that is genuinely partial. `clarify_topic_workflow` concatenates the router's free-text rationale with the user's message and tests remote_work first, so an incidental "remote work" in the rationale walks the whole remote-work slot order. On the published run amb-001 ("Can I take some time off?") was answered with amb-002's answer verbatim — asking for a destination country the item never needed. The judge passed it on "named missing information", so the flagship 1.000 (n=3) and design-and-evaluation.md:1081's "all three ambiguous items name every missing detail" both rest on an off-topic question. It is also the most demo-visible path in the section.
evidence: evaluation/results/r_1790074972_baseline.json: amb-001 and amb-002 carry byte-identical answers — "Happy to check — where would you be working from? I will also need to know how long you would be there, and from when." — while evaluation/dataset.yaml has amb-001 = "Can I take some time off?" with clarification_expects "the requested dates and the number of days" and amb-002 = "Am I allowed to work from there for a while?". Code: src/hrmosaic/agent/orchestrator.py:296-305, :382-400, :2921. The covering test (tests/unit/test_clarification_names_every_missing_slot.py:215-222) drives amb-001 from a fixture whose scripted rationale says "No dates were given…", so the branch is never exercised. The flip is nondeterministic across committed runs on one build: amb-001 got the correct question in r_1790067656 and r_1790075830.
fix: Test the user's message first and fall back to the rationale: `clarify_topic_workflow(turn.request.message) or clarify_topic_workflow(decision.rationale_summary)` (two calls, not one concatenation) — amb-002's own message contains "work from" so it is unaffected. Add a unit test whose scripted rationale mentions remote work on a "time off" question and asserts the dates/day-count question. Then either re-drive the three ambiguous items and republish, or soften design-and-evaluation.md:1081 to state that amb-001's question also asked for a destination it did not need.
effort: 45 min for the fix + test; +12 min and ~$0.8 if you re-drive the baseline

title: Task 1's DEMO.6 ① chain and timing budget were never migrated off the superseded 2026-09-15 capture
why_it_costs_marks: DEMO.6 is the most heavily graded beat of the recording, and the script tells the presenter to read `get_policy_section` off the waterfall in seq order — the run the script itself pins has no such call. The segment-table budget quotes 46.8 s over 35 spans against the pinned run's 38.2 s over 39 spans. On camera the presenter is hunting for a span that is not there.

The same document at :186 pins the 2026-09-22 transcript for beat ④, so the script contradicts itself about which run is "the pinned live run". docs/evidence/README.md:44 still attributes the script's timings and citation breadth to the 2026-09-15-p29 run; docs/process/sdd/G5-grade-5/task-7a-report.md:26 repeats the wrong chain.
fix: Re-cut ① from docs/evidence/demo-task-1-live-2026-09-22.txt: drop `get_policy_section` or hedge it the way task 2 ① already hedges `search_policy_documents` ("may or may not appear"), and change :72 to "Budget the turn itself at ~40 s: the run pinned on this build took 38.2 s over 39 spans; an earlier 2026-09-15 run took 46.8 s, so allow up to 50 s." Sweep docs/evidence/README.md:44 and the task-7a report too.

title: The script's pre-take warm-up check on /dashboard/evals cannot pass
why_it_costs_marks: The presenter is told to confirm the Runs table "fronts r_1790074972_baseline" before recording. The table is ordered newest-first and the ablation arms are always driven after the baseline, so the baseline is structurally the third row. Right now the table fronts the unjudged no_structured_tools arm, whose row reads "not judged" for groundedness and citation accuracy and strict pass 0.786. A presenter who takes the instruction seriously is troubleshooting a non-defect minutes before the take.

Ordering is unconditional: src/hrmosaic/web/dashboard.py:2818 `ORDER BY created_at DESC`; evaluation/ablation.py:39-40 `VARIANT_ORDER = ("baseline", "dense_only_k2", "no_structured_tools")`. Live GET /api/eval/runs returns r_1790075830_no_structured_tools, then r_1790075436_dense_only_k2, then r_1790074972_baseline.

title: deployed.md's cost row publishes a total the repo's own artifacts contradict
why_it_costs_marks: deployed.md:439 reads "$6.84 across the twelve committed evaluation runs … well inside §9.8's 'under $10 all-in'", in a file whose stated premise (deployed.md:3-5) is that every number was measured. There are now 22 committed run files summing to $13.98, so the count, the total and the budget headline are all falsified by one loop over evaluation/results/r_*.json. No rubric line caps model spend, but the self-audit claim is the point.
evidence: Verified: 22 files, est_cost_usd sum = 13.98. The first twelve chronologically sum to 6.841240, so the row was correct when dated 2026-09-11 and was never re-derived after ten more runs landed. The wave's own ledger measured the overage (docs/process/sdd/G5-grade-5/task-6b-report.md:59, "≈$5 total") without publishing it. "under $10 all in" is also asserted as built at docs/requirements-traceability.md:55 and :139, and five times in the design spec.
fix: Re-derive the row from the committed files (22 runs, $13.98, plus the live demo turns) and either restate the budget or say plainly that the wave's extra sweeps took measured spend past the spec's $10 expectation and why that was accepted. Sum is mechanical — have scripts/check_facts.py compute it and compare against the figure in deployed.md so it cannot rot.

title: The graded corpus table comes from a second parser and disagrees with the deployed index on screen
why_it_costs_marks: design-and-evaluation.md:151's headline ("64.2 pages, 31,007 words") and its 14-row table come from scripts/corpus_stats.py, which imports check_facts.py's script-local reader and counts markdown `##` markers and TXT underlines as words plus heading-only sections. The pipeline that builds the index — and the live corpus API and /dashboard/corpus — says 30,840 words, 63.7 pages, 176 sections. Ten of fourteen Sections figures differ (PTO and Remote published as 18 against the index's 15). Both readings pass the 30-120 page band, but the design walkthrough and the live Corpus page contradict each other on camera, against a project thesis that every number traces to a committed artifact.
evidence: Committed index (data/index/hr_index.sqlite documents table) and `hrmosaic.rag.parse.parse_corpus` both sum to 176 / 30,840 / 63.7; `.venv/bin/python scripts/corpus_stats.py` prints 14 files · 64.2 pages · 31,007 words, matching design-and-evaluation.md:154-168 row for row. Root cause: scripts/check_facts.py:236-252 uses raw file bytes for md/txt; src/hrmosaic/rag/parse/__init__.py:146-150 drops empty-bodied sections. CHANGELOG.md carries both figures (:41 = 31,007, :175 = 30,840) unreconciled. Ranked 27 in the prior card with the fix "point corpus_stats.py at parse_corpus"; task-6b-report.md:40 recorded it "verified unchanged".
fix: Repoint scripts/corpus_stats.py at `hrmosaic.rag.parse.parse_corpus` (keep check_facts' reader only for verbatim-quote matching), re-run it, repaste the table and headline in design-and-evaluation.md and note the correction in CHANGELOG. Add a contract test asserting the design-doc table equals `corpus_stats.py --json`. Also fix synthesize.j2:12's "median 995" (manifest median is 990.5).

title: "Full-history gitleaks scan" is claimed in README, ci.yml and narrated on camera, but a push scans two commits
why_it_costs_marks: README.md:166 calls the lint job "a full-history gitleaks scan", ci.yml:42 annotates the step `# full history`, and docs/demo-script.md:76 has the presenter say "gitleaks over full history" while the Actions log on screen says otherwise. gitleaks-action@v2 only runs an unbounded detect on dispatch/schedule; on the graded push it scanned 2 commits / 6.56 KB. The history really is clean, so this is claim accuracy — but it is stated in the graded README and spoken aloud.
evidence: Graded push run 35739263524 step log: `--log-opts=--no-merges --first-parent 3aa6650^..2dee277` → "2 commits scanned. … scanned ~6556 bytes (6.56 KB) … no leaks found". Dispatch run 35733516645 → "278 commits scanned … 13.22 MB … no leaks found". ci.yml:3-12 has no `schedule` trigger. The same overclaim also sits at design-and-evaluation.md:761/:837, docs/requirements-traceability.md:67 and ai-tooling.md:282. CHANGELOG.md:885 already states the truth, so the distinction was known.
fix: Either add an explicit whole-repo step to the lint job (`gitleaks detect --no-git=false`) so the claim becomes literally true on every run, or reword all six sites to "a gitleaks scan of the pushed commits, and of the whole history on a manual dispatch (last full scan 2026-09-22, clean)" — and change the demo-script line with them.

title: The published MCP tool schema advertises a retrieval threshold default the server never uses
why_it_costs_marks: `search_policy_documents` publishes `min_dense_score` with `"default": 0.26` in the committed schema and in design-and-evaluation.md:603's tool listing, but an omitted argument routes to `settings.min_support_score` = 0.45. 0.26 is specifically the pre-calibration value the project documents as having sat below the embedder's cosine floor. A grader reading the tool schema to understand filtering (R3.1) and gate calibration (R3.4) reads the wrong number next to :649's MIN_SUPPORT_SCORE (0.45), with nothing reconciling them; the model's own view of its tool is wrong the same way.
evidence: mcp/tools/search_policy_documents.schema.json:69 `"default": 0.26`; src/hrmosaic/mcpserver/tools/search_policy_documents.py:189 signature default 0.26 and :196 `threshold = min_dense_score if call.supplied(...) else settings.min_support_score`; src/hrmosaic/settings.py:110 default 0.45; .env.example:51 MIN_SUPPORT_SCORE=0.45. Also published at docs/architecture.html:1535 and recorded as 0.26 in tests/fixtures/traces/*.json retrieval spans. The ledger lists it as a deferred minor.
fix: Make the parameter `float | None = None` with `settings.min_support_score` as the documented effective default (the idiom already exists at src/hrmosaic/rag/retrieve.py:125,133), regenerate with scripts/gen_tool_schemas.py, repaste design-and-evaluation.md:603, and sweep docs/architecture.html:1535 and the two trace fixtures.

title: `paths-ignore` means the submission commit — pasting the demo-video URL into README — runs no CI and triggers no deploy
why_it_costs_marks: ci.yml:7 excludes `docs/**` and `*.md` from the push trigger. The last commit before submission is by design a root-level README edit (README.md:11 is the video placeholder), so it will run no lint, no test, no docs contract tests and no deploy: the graded tip will again carry no green run and the live sha will lag HEAD, re-opening prior gap 22 the wave just closed. It also means the docs contract tests — the guards against exactly the stale-claim class above — never gate the commits most likely to introduce them, and in practice docs commits go straight to main (3 merges total, no pre-commit hooks, 20 of the last 30 commits docs-only).
evidence: ci.yml:4-7 `paths-ignore: ['evaluation/results/**','evaluation/REPORT.md','docs/**','*.md']`. `git show --stat 2dee277` → 2 files, both under docs/process/sdd/; the tip only carries a run because the push bundled the CSS commit 3aa6650. docs/pre-submission-checklist.md has no step to dispatch ci.yml or re-read /health after the video commit.
fix: Keep the ratified filter (it protects Render build minutes) but add one line to docs/pre-submission-checklist.md: after the README video commit, `gh workflow run ci.yml -f deploy_only=true` and re-read `/health.app.git_sha`. Cheaper still, drop `*.md` alone so root-level docs run the suite.

title: The published run contains one genuinely wrong policy answer, and no rail catches a cited-but-contradicted claim
why_it_costs_marks: Against "correct, cited, grounded responses … at an outstanding level" there is a measured shortfall: citation accuracy 0.875 against resolvability 1.000, two items with claims the judge marked contradicted and one unsupported, and equipment-001 at groundedness 0.688 applying the Requesting-Additional-Equipment USD 500 director threshold to a 36-month refresh. G2 checks resolvability, not entailment, so a claim that is cited, resolvable and contradicted by the very chunk it cites survives all six rails (blocks_dropped_by_g2 = 0 for the whole run). Honestly disclosed, which is why it is not higher.
evidence: evaluation/results/r_1790074972_baseline.json: citation_accuracy_mean 0.8752, groundedness_mean 0.9633 (n=18), cit_resolve_mean 1.0 (n=28); equipment-001 per_claim {c4: contradicted, c5: unsupported}, groundedness 0.6875, passed 0; expenses-002 0.7857. corpus/equipment-and-asset.md:43 (automatic refresh ticket) vs :60 (the USD 500 rule); corpus/rules.yml:394-400 carries the threshold with no applies_when, so gold, rules engine and model all conflate it. Disclosed at design-and-evaluation.md:1441-1455.
fix: Editorial: decide in corpus/equipment-and-asset.md and corpus/rules.yml whether a priced refresh is a request, re-author equipment-001's gold against it, and add one clause to the guardrail section — "G2 checks resolvability, not entailment; a cited-but-contradicted claim is caught only by the judge" — so the table cannot be read as claiming more than it does.
effort: 45 min (corpus + gold + one sentence); re-drive optional

title: `catalog_sha` is `[REDACTED]` on every turn while four documents advertise it as span content
why_it_costs_marks: `catalog_sha` is a 64-char sha256 hex digest, and core/redact.py:49's long-base64 value pattern matches it, so core/trace.py:335 replaces it before persistence. mcp/README.md:67, design-and-evaluation.md:344 and four docs/architecture.html nodes all list it among what the discovery span records, and the prior card cited it as a §5 strength. The team found the symptom downstream (dashboard/mcp.html:8-9 notes the column "was [REDACTED] on every row") but corrected no document and exempted no key. The covering test passes vacuously.
evidence: `redact({'catalog_sha': hashlib.sha256(...).hexdigest()})` → `{'catalog_sha': '[REDACTED]'}`; decoding the mcp_discovery span in docs/evidence/demo-task-2-live-2026-09-15-session.json yields `catalog_sha: '[REDACTED]'`. tests/integration/test_audit_completeness.py:49 asserts the value is truthy and "[REDACTED]" is truthy; fixtures use a 16-char fake sha that escapes the regex.
fix: Short-circuit the value sweep for the digest keys (`catalog_sha`, `corpus_sha256`, `manifest_sha256`) — note PRESERVED_KEYS alone will not do it, since redact_text applies value patterns regardless of key — or tighten the base64 pattern to require a non-hex character. Then assert `len(payload['catalog_sha']) == 64` and regenerate the fixtures with a real digest. If it is to stay redacted, delete it from the four documents.

title: Safety, escalation and per-workflow evidence each rest on a single dataset item
why_it_costs_marks: Action-safety pass rate is 1.000 over n=1, each demo workflow's completion is 1.00 over n=1, escalation is one sensitive item, clarification is n=3. Every one is published with its n and labelled an indicator rather than a rate, which is the right treatment — but band 5's "excellent evaluation results covering … safety" is being asked to accept a safety denominator of one on precisely the confirmation-gate and escalation paths the rubric cares most about. The runner already evaluates the four safety clauses on all 28 turns and publishes only the narrowed denominator.
evidence: r_1790074972_baseline n_scored: safety 1, action_safety_pass_rate 1, workflow:pto_request 1, workflow:remote_work_eligibility 1, clarification 3. evaluation/dataset.yaml: unsafe_action 1, sensitive 1. evaluation/runner.py:518 scores the clauses per turn; :556-561 narrows the published denominator. docs/optimization-log.md names this as what the wave did not get.
fix: Add 2-3 unsafe_action items (draft_hr_email as a second write tool, a cancel-at-the-gate path, a confirm-then-perform path) and a second sensitive item, then re-drive — the write path already exists, so the cost is one sweep. Failing that, publish the per-turn four-clause pass rate as a second, larger safety denominator beside the n=1 figure.

title: A committed history run publishes a judge-agreement figure folded from another run's answers, and the live dashboard renders it
why_it_costs_marks: r_1790067656_baseline (committed "as history" in this wave) carries judge_agreement_rate 1.0 / n 8, folded from the pre-turn_id label file whose labels were authored against r_1789555212_baseline's served answers — exactly the class the design doc says "is not published" (it discloses the analogous r_1789069158 case but not this one). title: Stale figures inside the graded narrative: catalog_reopened_rate 0.038, the pto_request predicate, RSS 293.6
why_it_costs_marks: Three small hand-written figures outside the script-managed EVAL-NUMBERS block, in a document whose premise is that every number comes from a committed artifact. design-and-evaluation.md:460 says `catalog_reopened_rate` is "0.038 on the published run" — it is 0.000 (0.0385 belongs to the 26-item 2026-09-10/11 runs), and line 982 of the same file prints the correct 0.000. :474 states pto_request's `is_complete` without the `lookup_employee_profile` clause the code requires, in the one table documenting R4.2. :43's mermaid node carries an undated "293.6 MB live" against a live 303.8.

Live /health rss_mb 303.8 against the undated diagram label; every dated sibling (deployed.md:520, design-and-evaluation.md:1486) is stamped 2026-09-10.

why_it_costs_marks: design-and-evaluation.md:5 labels docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-08-hr-agentic-rag-design.md "Design source of truth" and README.md:19-20 links it as "the full design spec", with no note that it is pre-implementation. title: A red `ux` job (299 tests) does not block the deploy, so main carries red runs that shipped
why_it_costs_marks: §8's bullet reads "Deployment must only occur if tests pass". The ux job carries no `needs:` and nothing needs it, so deploy ships when it is red — run 35723846982 is the demonstration (ux failure, deploy success, overall conclusion failure). The rationale is documented three times and defensible, and the tip is fully green, but a grader scanning main's history sees red runs that reached production, and README's CI/CD paragraph (README.md:164-173) enumerates lint/test/docker/deploy without mentioning ux at all.
evidence: ci.yml:87-93 ("`needs:` is deliberately absent") and :146 `needs: [test, docker]`. `gh run view 35723846982` → ux failure, deploy success. Counter-evidence that the gate is real: run 35733477527 (test success, ux failure, deploy failure) and docs/evidence/ci-deploy-skipped.png.
fix: Either add `ux` to the deploy `needs:` (it ran ~11 min on the tip and is cached) or mark it `continue-on-error: true` with a job summary, so a red main run always means something that gates production is broken. Name the choice in README's CI/CD paragraph, which currently omits the job.

title: MCP record-vs-doc drift: null session id, "exactly one discovery span per turn", and an overstated retry
why_it_costs_marks: Three small inaccuracies in the documents a grader reads to check the MCP integration. `mcp_session_id` is always null because agent/client.py:445 reads `getattr(session, "session_id", None)` and mcp 2.2.0's ClientSession has no such attribute (the id lives on the transport the streamable-HTTP client never yields) — while four documents list it as recorded. mcp/README.md:65 and design-and-evaluation.md:343 assert in bold "exactly one mcp_discovery span per turn", which is false on the confirmation-resume path — i.e. demo task 2, the turn a grader is most likely to open. mcp/README.md:136 says a transport failure is retried once; only discovery is retried, and design-and-evaluation.md:411 words the same row correctly.
evidence: `hasattr(ClientSession,'session_id')` → False; docs/evidence/demo-task-1-live-2026-09-15-session.json shows `"mcp_session_id":null`, while mcp/README.md:232 records that the external handshake returned an `mcp-session-id` header. docs/evidence/demo-task-2-live-2026-09-22.txt shows mcp_discovery at seq 1 and seq 27 in one 36-span turn (orchestrator.py:3387 re-discovers on resume). agent/client.py:531-534 has no retry loop; the single re-discovery is orchestrator.py:1557-1563.
fix: Drop `mcp_session_id` from McpDiscoveryPayload and the four documents (or capture it via an httpx response hook); reword to "one mcp_discovery span per turn pass — a turn resumed after a confirmation carries a second"; and change mcp/README.md:136 to "the client re-discovers once at the discovery step; a tools/call that fails degrades the turn immediately".

title: Source docstrings and the traceability matrix still say "two declarative workflows"; three are registered
why_it_costs_marks: src/hrmosaic/agent/router.py:44 says "The two declarative workflows of §9.3" directly above a three-member `Literal`, and workflows/__init__.py:1 and :11 say "two" and "Both predicates below" where three follow. docs/requirements-traceability.md R4.2 names only two, so `expense_claim` appears in neither the traceability row nor `workflow_completion_by_workflow`, and no test ever observes its `is_complete` returning True (instrumented across 2,547 unit+integration tests: 20 calls, all False). Prior gap 27 carried the fix "say three" and it was worked only in the docs files.
